author: reek
body: The allow half of the scope check for the console family. Everything here sits inside the scope its signature grants, so it compiles and runs. The refusal half -- for the console channel and for the network authority both -- is codex/test/errors/scope-network-port.

author: reek
body: A console grant is a CHANNEL, not a path prefix. The channel is decided by which function was called and never by an argument the caller computed, so this is the one scoped check that cannot be defeated by an unprovable argument: print-error-uni is stderr no matter what it is handed.

author: reek
body: A signature that grants Console.Write "stdout" therefore admits print-line-uni and refuses print-error-uni, and the parent row Console admits both -- which is what every program in the tree that declares a bare [Console] relies on.

author: reek
body: THERE IS NO NETWORK HALF HERE, AND THAT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. The network scope relation is real and enforced -- the errors test proves it refuses a wrong port and a suffixed host -- but the operations it scopes (fetch, post, resolve-dns) are declared in Foreword chapter Network with no handler anywhere in the tree, so a program that calls one cannot be emitted (CDX2040) and the ALLOW direction cannot be exercised end to end by anybody.
